draft:
Bloom Nutrition is a London-headquartered premium women's nutrition brand offering an evidence-based supplement range across four primary categories: hormonal balance, energy and recovery, skin and hair health, and pregnancy and postnatal nutrition. The proposed transaction values Bloom at an enterprise value of EUR 310 million for a 72 percent stake.

The unit economics are exceptional for a brand at this stage. Trailing twelve months revenue is EUR 64 million, up from EUR 19 million in 2022 — a 47 percent compound annual growth rate. Gross margin is 71.4 percent and EBITDA margin is 32.8 percent. Customer acquisition cost payback is 5.2 months on first-purchase margin, and 87 percent of revenue comes from repeat customers. Channel mix is approximately 64 percent direct-to-consumer, 19 percent Amazon, 14 percent premium wholesale, and 3 percent clinic channel.

The Company was founded in 2018 by Sarah Whitmore and Dr. Lara Bennett, both Cambridge-trained scientists. Bloom is supported by a clinical advisory board of seven specialists across endocrinology, nutrition, and women's health. Product development cadence is two new product launches per year, supported by in-house formulation capability and contract manufacturing through GMP-certified European facilities.

Our investment thesis rests on the structural attractiveness of premium women's health (a EUR-denominated category growing at approximately 14 percent annually), Bloom's defensible product credibility and brand position, and a clear international runway in France, Italy, Spain, and selectively in the US over a five-year hold. Base case revenue growth from EUR 64 million to approximately EUR 195 million by 2030 generates 2.9x MOIC and 24 percent IRR.

The principal risks are customer acquisition cost inflation in direct-to-consumer (Bloom's payback has lengthened from 3.8 months in 2022 to 5.2 months today), founder-dependency on Sarah Whitmore who is closely associated with the brand, and the regulatory environment for women's health nutrition claims, which is becoming more demanding across European markets.
